The '''55th Academy Awards''' ceremony, organized by the [[Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences]] (AMPAS), honored [[1982 in film|films released in 1982]] and took place on April 11, 1983, at the [[Dorothy Chandler Pavilion]] in Los Angeles beginning at 6:00&nbsp;p.m. [[Pacific Time Zone|PST]] / 9:00&nbsp;p.m. [[Eastern Time Zone|EST]]. During the ceremony, AMPAS presented [[Academy Awards]] (commonly referred to as Oscars) in 24 categories. The ceremony, televised in the United States by [[American Broadcasting Company|ABC]], was produced by [[Howard W. Koch]] and directed by [[Marty Pasetta]].<ref name="Pasetta">{{harvnb|Osborne|2013|p=413}}</ref> Actors [[Walter Matthau]], [[Liza Minnelli]], [[Dudley Moore]], and [[Richard Pryor]] hosted the show. Matthau and Pryor hosted the gala for the second time; the former was a co-host of the [[48th Academy Awards|48th ceremony]] in 1976 while the latter co-hosted the [[49th Academy Awards|49th ceremony]] held in 1977.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Sundby |first1=Alex |title=Who Hosted the 2024 Oscars, and Who Hosted Past Academy Awards Ceremonies? |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/oscars-host-2024/ |access-date=October 2, 2024 |agency=[[CBS News]] |date=March 10, 2024 |archive-date=August 31, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240831133808/https://www.cbsnews.com/news/oscars-host-2024/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Conrad |first1=Michael |title=A Gentle Man |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/florence-morning-news-a-gentle-man/172415608/ |access-date=March 12, 2023 |archive-date=May 30, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250530091258/https://www.newspapers.com/article/florence-morning-news-a-gentle-man/172415608/ |work=[[The Morning News (American newspaper)|The Morning News]] |date=March 26, 1983 |page=41 |via=[[Ancestry.com|Newspapers.com]] |url-status=live }}</ref> Meanwhile, Minnelli and Moore hosted for the first time.<ref>{{cite news |title=Names in the News: 'Welk Doing Devil's Work' |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-vancouver-sun-names-in-the-news/172334097/ |access-date=January 15, 2024 |work=[[Vancouver Sun]] |date=March 2, 1983 |page=D16 |via=[[Ancestry.com|Newspapers.com]] }}</ref> Two weeks earlier, in a ceremony held at [[The Beverly Hilton]] in [[Beverly Hills, California]], on March 27, the [[Academy Scientific and Technical Awards]] were presented by host [[Dyan Cannon]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Past Scientific & Technical Awards Ceremonies|url=http://www.oscars.org/awards/scitech/pastawards.html|access-date=July 31, 2013 |publisher=[[Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140213185729/http://www.oscars.org/awards/scitech/pastawards.html|archive-date=February 13, 2014}}</ref>

''[[Gandhi (film)|Gandhi]]'' won eight awards, including [[Academy Award for Best Picture|Best Picture]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Shales |first1=Tom |author-link=Tom Shales |title=And the Winners Are... ''Gandhi'', Best Picture, Sweeps Oscars |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/lifestyle/1983/04/12/and-the-winners-are-gandhi-best-picture-sweeps-oscars/3c98414d-8bbb-4a52-b200-b7ec438e0368/ |access-date=March 23, 2023 |work=The Washington Post |date=April 11, 1983 |archive-date=August 28, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170828061229/https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/lifestyle/1983/04/12/and-the-winners-are-gandhi-best-picture-sweeps-oscars/3c98414d-8bbb-4a52-b200-b7ec438e0368/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Other winners included ''[[E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial]]'' with four awards, ''[[An Officer and a Gentleman]]'' with two, ''[[Begin the Beguine (film)|Begin the Beguine]]'', ''[[If You Love This Planet]]'', ''[[Just Another Missing Kid]]'', ''[[Missing (1982 film)|Missing]]'', ''[[Quest for Fire (film)|Quest for Fire]]'', ''[[A Shocking Accident]]'', ''[[Sophie's Choice (film)|Sophie's Choice]]'', ''[[Tango (1981 film)|Tango]]'', ''[[Tootsie]]'', and ''[[Victor/Victoria]]'' with one. The telecast garnered 53.2&nbsp;million viewers in the United States.

==Winners and nominees== 
The nominees for the 55th Academy Awards were announced on February 17, 1983, by Academy president [[Fay Kanin]] and actor [[Karl Malden]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Thomas |first1=Bob |title=''Gandhi'' Scores 11 Oscar Nominations |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-indianapolis-star-oscar-nominations/173452241/ |access-date=January 24, 2023 |archive-date=May 30, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250530091229/https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-indianapolis-star-oscar-nominations/173452241/ |work=[[The Indianapolis Star]] |date=February 18, 1983 |page=35 |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |url-status=live }}</ref> ''Gandhi'' received the most nominations with eleven total; ''[[Tootsie]]'' came in second with ten.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Arnold |first1=Gary |title=''Gandhi'' Tops Oscar Nominations |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/lifestyle/1983/02/18/gandhi-tops-oscar-nominations/2985e90f-7b7f-4e5c-b274-5ef0e4cbba97/ |access-date=March 12, 2023 |work=[[The Washington Post]] |date=February 18, 1983 |archive-date=August 28, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170828075001/https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/lifestyle/1983/02/18/gandhi-tops-oscar-nominations/2985e90f-7b7f-4e5c-b274-5ef0e4cbba97/ |url-status=live }}</ref> The winners were announced at the awards ceremony on April 11. Best Supporting Actress winner [[Jessica Lange]] was the second actress to earn both lead and supporting acting nominations in the same year after [[Teresa Wright]] who earned a nomination for Best Actress for 1942's ''[[The Pride of the Yankees]]'' while winning Best Supporting Actress in the same year for ''[[Mrs. Miniver]]''.<ref>{{harvnb|Wiley|Bona|1996|p=1142}}</ref> [[Louis Gossett Jr.]] became the first African-American winner for Best Supporting Actor.<ref>{{harvnb|Kinn|Piazza|2002|p=233}}</ref>

==Ceremony information==
{{multiple image|perrow = 2|total_width=300
| image1 = Walter Matthau - 1952.jpg
| alt1   = Walter Matthau in 1952
| image2 = Liza Minnelli Publicity 1973.jpg
| alt2  = Liza Minnelli in 1973
| image3 = Dudley Moore (cropped).jpg
| alt3   = Dudley Moore in 1999
| image4 = Richard Pryor (1986) (cropped).jpg
| alt4   = Richard Pryor in 1986
| footer = [[Walter Matthau]] (top left), [[Liza Minnelli]] (top right), [[Dudley Moore]] (bottom left), and [[Richard Pryor]] (bottom right) hosted the 55th Academy Awards.
}}

In October 1982, the Academy hired film producer [[Howard W. Koch]] to produce the ceremony for the eighth time. "I am delighted that the Academy will have the benefit  of Howard Koch's experience  and creativity again this year," said AMPAS President [[Fay Kanin]] in a press release announcing the selection. "We are extremely proud of the Awards programs Howard has produced for us in years past, and look forward to an equally graceful and exciting presentation this year.<ref>{{cite web |title=Howard W. Koch to Produce 55th Academy Awards Show |url=https://digitalcollections.oscars.org/digital/collection/p15759coll9/id/7529/rec/1 |publisher=[[Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences]] |access-date=March 12, 2023 |archive-date=May 30, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250530095709/https://web.archive.org/screenshot/https://digitalcollections.oscars.org/digital/collection/p15759coll9/id/7529/rec/1 |date=October 18, 1982 |url-status=live }}</ref> Five months later, it was announced that actors [[Walter Matthau]], [[Liza Minnelli]], [[Dudley Moore]], and [[Richard Pryor]] would share hosting duties for the gala.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Beck |first1=Marilyn |author-link=Marilyn Beck |title=Hepburn to Pair Up with Nolte |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-daily-breeze-marilyn-beck-entertainm/172333909/ |access-date=September 18, 2023 |archive-date=May 30, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250530100154/https://web.archive.org/screenshot/https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-daily-breeze-marilyn-beck-entertainm/172333909/ |work=[[Daily Breeze]] |date=March 5, 1983 |page=B3 |via=[[Ancestry.com|Newspapers.com]] |url-status=live }}</ref> According to news reports, AMPAS originally sought late night talk show host [[Johnny Carson]] to emcee the festivities again, but he declined the offer due to Carson having personal issues related to the recent breakup with his wife.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Caulfield |first1=Deborah |title=Psst, Buddy...Wanna See a Pre-Release Script |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-los-angeles-times-psst-buddywann/172415395/ |access-date=July 12, 2023 |archive-date=May 30, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250530091358/https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-los-angeles-times-psst-buddywann/172415395/ |work=[[Los Angeles Times]] |date=March 21, 1983 |page=55 |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |url-status=live }}</ref> 

[[Marty Pasetta]] directed the telecast; [[Bill Conti]] served as conductor and musical director.<ref name="Pasetta" /> Actor [[John Moschitta Jr.]], who was known for his fast talking delivery in commercials, made an appearance at the beginning of the ceremony explaining the voting rules and procedures.<ref>{{harvnb|Wiley|Bona|1996|p=624}}</ref> Several members of the [[Naval Reserve Officers Training Corps]] from the [[University of Southern California]] made an appearance at the beginning of the performance of Best Original Song nominee "[[Up Where We Belong]]" from the film ''[[An Officer and a Gentleman]]''.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Buck |first1=Jerry |title=''Gandhi'' Humbly Steals Slow-Moving Oscars Show |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/santa-cruz-sentinel-jerry-buck-oscar-rev/172333550/ |access-date=March 23, 2023 |archive-date=May 30, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250530091409/https://www.newspapers.com/article/santa-cruz-sentinel-jerry-buck-oscar-rev/172333550/ |work=[[Santa Cruz Sentinel]] |date=April 12, 1983 |page=A-9 |via=[[Ancestry.com|Newspapers.com]] |url-status=live }}</ref> [[Peter Allen (musician)|Peter Allen]] and [[Bernadette Peters]] performed a medley of songs in tribute to songwriter [[Irving Berlin]].<ref>{{harvnb|Wiley|Bona|1996|p=625}}</ref> [[Ethel Merman]] was initially slated to perform alongside Allen and Peters, but she cancelled her appearance after suffering a [[stroke]].<ref>{{harvnb|Osborne|2013|p=266}}</ref> 

===Box office performance of Best Picture nominees===
At the time of the nominations announcement on February 16, the combined gross of the five Best Picture nominees at the US box office was $496&nbsp;million.<ref name=BoxOfficeOscars>{{cite web |title=1982 Academy Award Nominations and Winner for Best Picture |url=https://boxofficemojo.com/oscar/chart/?yr=1982&p=.htm |access-date=June 17, 2014 |publisher=[[Box Office Mojo]] |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140614052209/http://boxofficemojo.com/oscar/chart/?yr=1982&p=.htm |archive-date=June 14, 2014}}</ref> ''E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial'' was the highest earner among the Best Picture nominees, with $329&nbsp;million in domestic box office receipts. The film was followed by ''Tootsie'' ($101&nbsp;million), ''The Verdict'' ($39.7&nbsp;million), ''Missing'' ($14&nbsp;million), and ''Gandhi'' ($11.9&nbsp;million).<ref name=BoxOfficeOscars/>

===Critical reviews===
Thomas Sabulis wrote in the ''[[Tampa Bay Times|St. Petersburg Times]]'', "The television show itself was one of the poorest academy presentations in recent memory." He also criticized production elements such as the opening number [[Kristy McNichol]] mispronouncing nominees names.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Sabulis |first1=Thomas |title=Dignity of ''Gandhi'' Key to Dominance |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/tampa-bay-times-55th-oscars-2/75829688/ |access-date=March 12, 2023 |archive-date=May 30, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250530094717/https://www.newspapers.com/article/tampa-bay-times-55th-oscars-2/75829688/ |work=[[Tampa Bay Times|St. Petersburg Times]] |date=April 13, 1983 |page=2-D |via=[[Ancestry.com|Newspapers.com]] |url-status=live }}</ref> Writing for the ''[[Austin American-Statesman]]'', Diane Holoway commented, "In the quarter of a century or so that I've been watching the gala event, this was the sloppiest production ever. And clocking in at well over three hours, it was one of the longest."<ref>{{cite news |last1=Holoway |first1=Diane |title=Academy Ails |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/austin-american-statesman-55th-oscars/75767886/ |access-date=January 24, 2023 |archive-date=May 30, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250530092035/https://www.newspapers.com/article/austin-american-statesman-55th-oscars/75767886/ |work=[[Austin American-Statesman]] |date=April 13, 1983 |page=B12 |via=[[Ancestry.com|Newspapers.com]] |url-status=live }}</ref> ''[[Mansfield News Journal]]'''s Ray Dyson commented, "The Academy Awards ceremony ran true to form Monday night. Every year when the biggest awards in moviedom are passed out there are two predictions that always come true — it will go too long and it will be boring." He praised the Irving Berlin tribute and actor John Moschitta's humorous and rapid recitation of the Academy voting rules, but found the telecast to be listless and filled with technical glitches.<ref name="Mansfield" />

Television critic [[Howard Rosenberg]] of ''[[Los Angeles Times]]'' wrote, "This telecast continues to be one of the best shows around, perhaps not as tightly produced as the [[Tony Awards|Tonys]], but unequaled for charisma and ogling charisma."<ref>{{cite news |last1=Rosenberg |first1=Howard |author-link=Howard Rosenberg |title=Oscars Show in Winner's Circle |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-los-angeles-times-la-times-oscars-ce/172415425/ |access-date=July 12, 2023 |archive-date=May 30, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250530090812/https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-los-angeles-times-la-times-oscars-ce/172415425/ |work=[[Los Angeles Times]] |date=April 13, 1983 |page=83 |via=[[Ancestry.com|Newspapers.com]] |url-status=live }}</ref> ''[[The New York Times]]'' film critic [[Vincent Canby]] said, The 55th presentation, last Monday night, was everything one could have wished it to be, including dignified." However, he criticized the decision to reward ''Gandhi'' with the Best Picture award saying, "''E.T.'' and ''Tootsie'' are films. ''Gandhi'' is a laboriously illustrated textbook."<ref>{{cite news |last1=Canby |first1=Vincent |author-link=Vincent Canby |title=Film View: Why We Watch the Academy Awards |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1983/04/17/movies/film-view-why-we-watch-the-academy-awards.html |access-date=March 12, 2023 |work=[[The New York Times]] |date=April 13, 1983 |archive-date=February 26, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230226035116/https://www.nytimes.com/1983/04/17/movies/film-view-why-we-watch-the-academy-awards.html |url-status=live }}</ref> ''[[The News & Observer]]'' entertainment editor Bill Morrison noted that the lack of suspense amongst the winners and repetitive "thank yous" in the acceptance speeches bogged down the ceremony, but he reserved praise for co-host Moore calling him "a delightful emcee."<ref>{{cite news |last1=Morrison |first1=Bill |title=Watching the Academy Awards Wasn't a Thankless Task |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-news-and-observer-55th-oscars/75774336/ |access-date=July 12, 2023 |archive-date=May 30, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250530111908/https://web.archive.org/screenshot/https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-news-and-observer-55th-oscars/75774336/ |work=[[The News & Observer]] |date=April 13, 1983 |page=9A |via=[[Ancestry.com|Newspapers.com]] |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Ratings and reception===
The American telecast on ABC drew in an average of 53.2 million people over the length of the entire ceremony.<ref name="Viewership">{{cite news|title=Top-10 Most Watched Academy Awards Broadcasts |url=https://www.nielsen.com/insights/2009/top-10-most-watched-academy-awards-broadcasts/ |publisher=[[Nielsen N.V.]] |date=February 18, 2009 |access-date=August 25, 2015 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160127130438/http://www.nielsen.com/us/en/insights/news/2009/top-10-most-watched-academy-awards-broadcasts.html |archive-date=January 27, 2016 }}</ref> Moreover, the show drew higher [[Nielsen Media Research|Nielsen ratings]] compared to the previous ceremony, with 38% of households watching with a 59% share.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Shister |first1=Gail |title=''Saturday Night'' and Murphy Returning Next Season |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-philadelphia-inquirer-saturday-night/172415458/ |access-date=January 24, 2023 |archive-date=May 30, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250530090521/https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-philadelphia-inquirer-saturday-night/172415458/ |work=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]] |date=April 20, 1983 |page=8-F |via=[[Ancestry.com|Newspapers.com]] |url-status=live }}</ref> In August 1983, the ceremony presentation received five nominations at the [[35th Primetime Emmy Awards|35th Primetime Emmys]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Margulies |first1=Lee |title=Again, NBC Is No. 1...at Emmy Time |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-los-angeles-times-emmy-award-nominat/172415668/ |access-date=July 12, 2023 |archive-date=May 30, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250530092812/https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-los-angeles-times-emmy-award-nominat/172415668/ |work=[[Los Angeles Times]] |date=August 5, 1983 |page=108 |via=[[Ancestry.com|Newspapers.com]] |url-status=live }}</ref> The following month, it won an award for Michael Corenblith and Ray Klausen's [[Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Production Design for a Variety, Reality or Competition Series|art direction]] of the program.<ref>{{cite web |title=55th Annual Academy Awards Presentation |url=https://www.televisionacademy.com/shows/55th-annual-academy-awards-presentation |publisher=[[Academy of Television Arts & Sciences]] |access-date=March 12, 2023 |archive-date=February 9, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250209153833/https://www.televisionacademy.com/shows/55th-annual-academy-awards-presentation |url-status=live }}</ref>
